title: Best Remix Producers (2026): Official Remixes and Edits
description: How to hire a remix producer for an official remix, club edit or new version of your song: stems, rights, how to brief it, price drivers and red flags.
intro: Remix producers create new versions of a song: dance remixes, slowed or acoustic versions, club edits or a whole new genre take. Remixes can bring a track to new audiences and playlists. Problems start when the remix uses songs you do not have rights to, the stems are poor quality, or ownership and royalties are not agreed. This guide helps you commission remixes you can release.

faq.a: Only songs you own or have permission to remix. Releasing a remix of someone else's song without a license can lead to takedowns.

faq.q: What do I need to send?
faq.a: Stems, which are separate tracks for vocals, drums, bass and other parts, plus the tempo and key.
Agree in writing. Often the original artist owns the remix and the remixer is paid a fee, but other arrangements exist.

faq.q: Will the remix be mixed and mastered?
faq.a: Ask. Some producers deliver a finished master; others deliver a mix for separate mastering.

faq.q: Can I get extended or radio versions?
faq.a: Many producers offer extended club mixes, radio edits and instrumentals. Request them upfront.
